Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 01] Weekly Subscription Grants Permanent Non-Expiring Lifetime Pro Access
Current behavior: persistEntitlement writes source = "play_billing" without planId or expiresAt; isLifetime evaluates to true when proExpiresAt is null
Expected behavior: Weekly purchases must store weekly plan ID and expire when not renewed; Lifetime must only be granted for verified lifetime non-consumables
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 01. Missing expiry no longer implies lifetime. PlanId, productId, and proExpiresAt stored in preferences. queryOwnedPurchases verifies purchases on startup with automatic revocation when expired. 263 unit tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: missing plan identity in persistEntitlement and fallback to Lifetime on null expiry
User impact: User receives unearned permanent Pro access after paying only ₹39 once
Business impact: Complete destruction of recurring subscription revenue model; ₹39 one-time payment eliminates all future weekly/monthly/yearly LTV
Recommended approach: Store verified planId and authoritative expiry in preferences; require explicit lifetime planId in EntitlementManager
Acceptance criteria: Unit and sandbox billing tests verify weekly plan expires after 7 days and reverts to Free tier
Testing requirements: Execute purchase of weekly plan; verify expiration timestamp is enforced and access expires when subscription ends

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 02] Main-Thread Synchronous PNG Compression & Disk Deletion in Notification Listener
Current behavior: processNotification executes on Main listener thread and synchronously calls Bitmap.compress(PNG 100) and directory.listFiles() deletions
Expected behavior: All image encoding and disk I/O should execute asynchronously on a background thread without blocking UI
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 02. Offloaded to NotificationArtworkRepository with 2-tier memory LRU + bounded disk cache on limitedParallelism(2) IO dispatcher. 10 automated stress tests pass (0 violations). Verified on Realme 8 hardware.
Root cause: Confirmed: synchronous file output stream compression on Main looper thread
User impact: System UI stutter, frame drops below 15fps, and potential NotificationListenerService ANR freeze
Business impact: Play Store 1-star reviews for lagging; ANR rate exceeding 0.47% bad behavior threshold
Recommended approach: Move image caching to Dispatchers.IO or an in-memory LruCache<String Bitmap> with async disk backup
Acceptance criteria: Zero disk I/O on Main thread during notification bursts; smooth 60fps scrolling
Testing requirements: Simulate 25 simultaneous notifications; verify zero StrictMode disk read/write violations

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 03] Manifest BroadcastReceiver Statelessness Breaks Call Workflow and Summary Dialog
Current behavior: Instance state variables in TelephonyStateReceiver are wiped on each broadcast transition (RINGING -> OFFHOOK -> IDLE)
Expected behavior: Call state and duration must persist across telephony transitions in a singleton CallSessionCoordinator
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 03. TelephonyStateReceiver refactored to stateless forwarder using goAsync(). CallSessionCoordinator provides thread-safe singleton state machine with monotonic clock tracking, OEM duplicate broadcast deduplication, and fallback notification dispatch. 20 automated tests pass. Verified on Realme 8 hardware.
Root cause: Confirmed: Android re-instantiates BroadcastReceiver per intent resetting all instance fields
User impact: User never receives post-call summary or shortcuts; call duration is reported as 0s; completed calls execute hangup logic
Business impact: Destroys primary daily retention engine; users assume call tracking is completely broken
Recommended approach: Hoist state into singleton CallSessionCoordinator with monotonic time tracking and pending intent fallbacks
Acceptance criteria: Physical call end triggers CallSummaryDialog with accurate duration and logs entry in CallHistoryRepository
Testing requirements: Receive incoming call, answer, stay offhook 15s, hang up; verify call summary displays with 15s duration

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 03] Inverted Call Summary Entitlement Gating in PremiumFeaturePolicy
Current behavior: callSummaryEnabled evaluates to !isProActive || requested, making feature enabled by default for Free users while UI marks it PRO
Expected behavior: Free users must have 100% control to opt out of call summary dialog, while Pro users unlock premium customization (timeout, custom quick actions)
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 03. Policy decoupled: callSummaryEnabled(isProActive, requested) strictly returns requested for all users. Added callSummaryCustomizationEnabled(isProActive) restricting timeout and advanced action settings to Pro. Automated unit tests verified.
Root cause: Confirmed: logical operator error in entitlement check
User impact: Free users see Call Summary as PRO in settings but cannot disable it; confusing UX state
Business impact: Undermines credibility of Pro feature gating and paywall value proposition
Recommended approach: Decouple toggle from Pro gating; preserve free opt-out and gate advanced customizations to Pro
Acceptance criteria: Policy and settings toggle are 100% consistent across Free and Pro user states
Testing requirements: Toggle call summary on Free and Pro accounts; verify matching behavior between settings and overlay

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 04] Play Store Rejection Risk: Unused CAMERA and LOCATION Permissions Declared in Manifest
Current behavior: AndroidManifest.xml requests CAMERA, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION but code never accesses camera sensors or GPS
Expected behavior: Manifest should declare only permissions genuinely required by runtime code (Google Play Data Minimization policy)
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 04. Pruned CAMERA, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, and camera feature tag from AndroidManifest.xml. Verified via aapt dump permissions on built APK: 0 camera or location permissions present. TelephonyStateReceiver protected with READ_PHONE_STATE permission.
Root cause: Confirmed: scaffolded permissions never pruned prior to release candidate
User impact: Users see invasive permission prompts on installation; trust degraded
Business impact: Google Play automated rejection for violating Data Minimization policy
Recommended approach: Remove CAMERA, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION from AndroidManifest.xml
Acceptance criteria: aapt dump permissions on release APK shows zero camera or location permission strings
Testing requirements: Run aapt dump permissions build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk; verify clean permission profile

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 04] Accessibility Service Declares Over-Privileged Gestures and Content Retrieval Flags
Current behavior: accessibility_service_config.xml declares canPerformGestures=true and canRetrieveWindowContent=true but code never uses them
Expected behavior: Configuration should set canPerformGestures=false, canRetrieveWindowContent=false, and drop typeWindowContentChanged
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 04. accessibility_service_config.xml hardened: canPerformGestures=false, canRetrieveWindowContent=false, and event types restricted to typeWindowStateChanged|typeWindowsChanged. IslandOverlayService onAccessibilityEvent refactored to eliminate window.root calls. Merged APK xmltree verified.
Root cause: Confirmed: default template copied without trimming unneeded capabilities
User impact: Users see scary system warning: "This service can observe all text you type including personal data"
Business impact: Google Play Developer Policy review rejection under Accessibility API guidelines
Recommended approach: Harden accessibility_service_config.xml to minimal required surface (window state only)
Acceptance criteria: Accessibility service passes Play Console automated declaration scanner without high-risk warnings
Testing requirements: Enable Accessibility Service on device; verify system warning does not claim text observation

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 05] Active Wi-Fi Discovery Scanning Runs Continuously 24/7 in Background Service
Current behavior: MediaRouteActivityMonitor registers MediaRouter with CALLBACK_FLAG_PERFORM_ACTIVE_SCAN continuously in background service
Expected behavior: MediaRouter discovery should use passive callbacks or unregister when media is not actively playing
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 05. Replaced CALLBACK_FLAG_PERFORM_ACTIVE_SCAN with passive route observation flag 0, stopping continuous mDNS and Wi-Fi multicast probing. Added isRegistered idempotency guard. Automated tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: active scan flag forces continuous mDNS and Wi-Fi multicast probing
User impact: Noticeable background battery consumption even when phone is locked in pocket
Business impact: High uninstall rate; negative Play Store reviews complaining about battery drain
Recommended approach: Remove CALLBACK_FLAG_PERFORM_ACTIVE_SCAN or unregister when no media is playing
Acceptance criteria: Device enters CPU deep sleep within 60s of screen-off; Wi-Fi multicast lock released
Testing requirements: Profile device idle battery drain with adb shell dumpsys batterystats over 2 hours

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 05] Continuous 1.5s Bluetooth Polling Loop Queries IPC and Prevents CPU Deep Sleep
Current behavior: BluetoothAccessoryMonitor runs a coroutine while(isActive) loop querying BluetoothManager.getConnectedDevices() every 1500ms
Expected behavior: Bluetooth connection state should be monitored reactively using BroadcastReceiver for BluetoothDevice.ACTION_ACL_CONNECTED
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 05. Removed 1.5s polling loop and POLL_INTERVAL_MILLIS. BluetoothAccessoryMonitor reads state once on start and reacts to system broadcasts and battery callbacks via systemIslandReceiver on Dispatchers.IO. Automated tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: polling loop used instead of event-driven broadcast listener
User impact: Device CPU unable to enter lowest power state; battery drain
Business impact: User complaints and OS "App consuming battery in background" warnings
Recommended approach: Replace polling loop with reactive BroadcastReceiver listening for ACL_CONNECTED / ACL_DISCONNECTED
Acceptance criteria: Zero Bluetooth IPC calls while device connection state is static
Testing requirements: Connect/disconnect Bluetooth headphones; verify island updates instantly with zero polling

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 05] Audio Volume Observer Checks Wrong Preference Key for Ringer Mode HUD
Current behavior: On ringer volume change code checks preferences.showVolumeIndicator.first() instead of preferences.showRingerModeIndicator.first()
Expected behavior: Ringer mode change should check showRingerModeIndicator
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 05. Decoupled Ringer HUD from showVolumeIndicator to showRingerModeIndicator in AudioVolumeObserver. Separated stream volume evaluation so ringer and media volume updates are never mutually blocked. Automated tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: copy-paste typo in preference key inspection
User impact: Ringer Mode HUD is silently blocked when user disables Volume HUD but enables Ringer HUD
Business impact: User thinks ringer feature is broken; negative reviews
Recommended approach: Update line 61 to inspect preferences.showRingerModeIndicator.first()
Acceptance criteria: Disabling Volume HUD while enabling Ringer HUD correctly displays ringer pill on mode toggle
Testing requirements: Turn off Volume HUD, turn on Ringer HUD, toggle physical ringer; verify HUD renders

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 06] WindowManager Touch Leak When Always-on-Top Disabled
Current behavior: Disabling Always on Top sets Compose alpha to 0f but leaves the transparent 1080x72px window attached without FLAG_NOT_TOUCHABLE
Expected behavior: When island is hidden or disabled, WindowManager should detach view or set FLAG_NOT_TOUCHABLE
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 06. Dynamic window params observer in IslandOverlayService sets FLAG_NOT_TOUCHABLE, width=0, height=0, and view INVISIBLE when OverlayDisplayPolicy.shouldRender() is false. Physical swipe down for status bar shade verified on Realme 8 hardware.
Root cause: Confirmed: Compose visibility does not alter WindowManager touch consumption flags
User impact: Users cannot pull down Android notification shade or tap app action bars beneath the island area
Business impact: Severe UX defect; users report touch screen is broken and uninstall app immediately
Recommended approach: Dynamically apply FLAG_NOT_TOUCHABLE when island is hidden or removeView from WindowManager
Acceptance criteria: Status bar touches pass through 100% cleanly when Always on Top is disabled
Testing requirements: Disable Always on Top; pull down notification shade from top of screen; verify gesture works

Current behavior: DisplaySettingsScreen saves preferences to DataStore, but IslandOverlayService and DynamicIslandPill never consume them
Expected behavior: Preferences saved in DisplaySettingsScreen must reactively update DynamicIslandPill layout and shader params
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 06. Recommended approach: Connect DataStore display keys to IslandOverlayService state machine and DynamicIslandPill
Acceptance criteria: Changing RGB color picker in settings immediately changes glow color on the live floating island
Testing requirements: Select Cyan neon color in settings; verify floating island renders cyan glow around cutout

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 02] Unsynchronized Multi-Dispatcher State Mutations in IslandStateManager Risk Race Conditions
Current behavior: IslandStateManager exposes 12 StateFlow streams mutated concurrently from IO, Main, and Default dispatchers without a mutex
Expected behavior: All state mutations should be confined to a dedicated serial dispatcher or protected by a single-threaded mutex
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 02. State mutations fully synchronized via stateLock monitor, with generational cancellation tokens (dismissTimerGeneration, liveActivityGenerations). Multi-threaded concurrency stress test (10 threads, 500 ops) verified 0 race conditions or crashes.
Root cause: Confirmed: concurrent updates to activeLiveActivities and notificationDeadlines maps
User impact: Temporary alerts get stuck or dismiss prematurely; random visual glitches in island pill
Business impact: Unreliable user experience; unpredictable island behavior during multi-event scenarios
Recommended approach: Confine IslandStateManager state mutations to Dispatchers.Main.immediate with serial job queue
Acceptance criteria: Stress test with 50 concurrent events produces zero ConcurrentModificationException crashes
Testing requirements: Launch 50 parallel coroutines updating island state; verify clean state resolution

Expected behavior: Lifetime should be priced at 2.5x-3.5x Annual (₹499-₹699) to protect recurring subscription LTV

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 06] Composition-Phase Animated Dp Reads in DynamicIslandPill Cause 60-120fps Recomposition
Current behavior: animatedWidth and animatedHeight use animateDpAsState and are read directly inside Box(modifier = Modifier.width().height())
Expected behavior: Animated dimensions should be applied via Modifier.layout to skip composition phase and execute in layout phase
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 06. Implemented layout-phase modifier Modifier.animatedIslandDimensions(widthProvider, heightProvider) via androidx.compose.ui.layout.layout on Bloom Box and Main Pill Body, skipping composition phase entirely during size animations. 314 unit tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: reading State<Dp> during composition rather than layout/draw phase
User impact: Janky animations, dropped frames, and thermal throttling on entry-level Android devices
Business impact: App feels unpolished compared to iOS Dynamic Island fluid 60fps spring animations
Recommended approach: Migrate from Modifier.width(animatedWidth) to Modifier.layout { measurable, constraints -> ... }
Acceptance criteria: Recomposition count during island expansion drops from 60+ to 0 for child content
Testing requirements: Profile island expansion animation in Layout Inspector; verify zero composition churn on children

User impact: Remote Config updates have zero effect on client app behavior; ad unit and trial changes fail

Acceptance criteria: Remote config fetches successfully parse currentremoteconfig.json without falling back

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 09] AdSurfacePolicy Inversion Suppresses In-App Ads for 7-Day Trial Users
Current behavior: AdSurfacePolicy tests !isProActive instead of !isAdFree suppressing ads during trials and rewarded passes
Expected behavior: In-app banner and native ads should show during 7-day install trial and rewarded passes (only Paid Pro is ad-free)

Refactored AdSurfacePolicy.shouldShowBanner/Native to accept isAdFree parameter decoupled from isProActive. 7-Day Trial and Rewarded Pass users have isPro = true, isAdFree = false, rendering banner and native ads as designed. Paid Pro users (isAdFree = true) completely suppress ads. Tested across 351 unit tests and verified on Realme 8 hardware.

User impact: Non-paying trial users see 0 ads for 7 days, eliminating ad monetization during peak adoption
Business impact: Loss of AdMob banner/native ad revenue during user acquisition spike
Recommended approach: Update AdSurfacePolicy to check !isAdFree to honor FEATURE_ENTITLEMENT_MATRIX.md

User impact: Marketers cannot determine which specific screen placement generates the highest ad ARPU
Business impact: Suboptimal ad placement decisions; unable to prune low-performing ad slots

Acceptance criteria: BigQuery ad_impression exports include distinct placement dimension for every ad impression

Expected behavior: Debug gallery and simulator screens should be quarantined behind BuildConfig.DEBUG guards

Business impact: Minor APK bloat and exposure of internal design token test harness

Acceptance criteria: Component gallery is completely unreachable in release build variant
Testing requirements: Build release APK; verify ComponentGallery route throws destination not found if triggered

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 07] Missing Android Messages & UPI Payment Priority Boost in NotificationReducer
Current behavior: Financial alerts and OTPs are treated as standard priority instead of high-priority temporary interrupts
Expected behavior: Payment alerts (GPay, PhonePe, Paytm) and OTP SMS should have elevated priority (Level 2) and 8s display
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 07. Integrated 14 UPI/banking packages and SMS packages, OTP regex, financial keywords, and recommendedDisplaySeconds guaranteeing 8s minimum duration. Integrated into NotificationReducer queue sorting and NotificationInterruptionPolicy. Tested across 324 unit tests and verified on Realme 8.

User impact: Users miss payment confirmations and have to manually expand island to copy OTP
Business impact: Degraded utility in India market where UPI payment soundbox confirmations are high value
Recommended approach: Add UPI app package whitelist and OTP pattern matcher to NotificationPriorityPolicy
Acceptance criteria: PhonePe payment alert immediately surfaces as elevated temporary HUD over music playback
Testing requirements: Simulate GPay payment notification while music is playing; verify temporary payment HUD takes priority

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 07] Regional UPI Payment Apps Lack Explicit PII Redaction in Lock Screen Privacy Policy
Current behavior: LockScreenPrivacyPolicy masks sender and body for WhatsApp/Telegram but lacks rule for UPI apps
Expected behavior: On lock screen, UPI balance details and transaction amounts should be masked to "Payment Received"
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 07. Mandated zero-PII financial safety contract in LockScreenPrivacyPolicy. When device is locked, transaction notifications are masked to text "Payment received", title appName/Transaction Alert, and expandedText "Unlock to view transaction details", stripping private balances, accounts, and actions. Tested across 324 unit tests.

User impact: Bystanders can see user private financial balance on ambient display
Business impact: User privacy risk; potential complaints in security-conscious user segments
Recommended approach: Add financial notification classifier that masks monetary amounts when keyguard is locked
Acceptance criteria: Lock screen displays "Payment Received" without showing account numbers or balances
Testing requirements: Simulate bank transaction notification on locked device; verify monetary balance is masked

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 07] Paused Media Remains Pinned in Compact State Indefinitely Instead of Timing Out
Current behavior: When user pauses media playback, compact trailing waveform continues to render until process death
Expected behavior: Paused media should auto-collapse to Idle after 3-5 seconds of paused state
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 07. Implemented 3.5-second auto-collapse timer (PAUSE_AUTO_COLLAPSE_DELAY_MS = 3500L) in both MediaPlaybackRegistry and IslandStateManager. When media playback transitions to PAUSED in compact mode, ticker job cancels and island smoothly returns to Minimal/Idle bounds. Tested across 324 unit tests.
Root cause: Confirmed: playbackState == STATE_PAUSED does not start a cleanup countdown timer
User impact: Island stays permanently expanded around notch, blocking normal compact idle state
Business impact: User annoyance; island feels "stuck" on old media tracks
Recommended approach: Add 3-second auto-collapse timer in MediaPlaybackRegistry when playback state changes to PAUSED
Acceptance criteria: Pausing media smoothly collapses island back to idle cutout within 3.5 seconds
Testing requirements: Play Spotify track, hit pause; verify island animates back to idle bounds after 3s

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 07] Media Classification Collision: Streaming Video Notifications Interfere with Music Island
Current behavior: YouTube / Netflix notifications with media controls override Spotify background playback in state manager
Expected behavior: Audio-only playback (Spotify, Apple Music) should have dedicated slot separate from video notifications
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 07. Classified audio-only vs video streaming packages, added canTakeOwnership enforcing audio-first session lock and 500ms hysteresis debounce on rapid session switching, and prioritized active audio controllers in IslandNotificationListener. Tested across 324 unit tests.
Root cause: Confirmed: single MediaPlaybackRegistry slot overwritten by any app with MediaSession
User impact: Visual flickering and erratic seekbar jumps when user switches between apps
Business impact: Poor perceived software quality; frustrating multi-media experience
Recommended approach: Implement primary audio session lock in MediaPlaybackRegistry prioritizing active audio streams
Acceptance criteria: Spotify playback maintains island ownership unless YouTube explicitly requests audio focus
Testing requirements: Play Spotify in background, open YouTube video; verify smooth audio focus transition

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 03] Call Summary Dialog Lacks Direct WhatsApp Deep-Link Action Chip
Current behavior: CallSummaryDialog only offers standard phone dialer callback and lacks 1-tap WhatsApp message action
Expected behavior: Call summary must include 1-tap WhatsApp message shortcut with E.164 normalization, domestic trunk stripping, and package fallback
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 03. CallActionLauncher formats WhatsApp numbers, targets com.whatsapp/w4b with fallback to wa.me URI. 5 quick action chips (Redial, SMS, WhatsApp, Save, Copy) integrated into CallSummaryDialog and DynamicIslandPill. Tested and verified on hardware.

User impact: Missed opportunity for high-frequency daily utility in India (WhatsApp primary communication)
Business impact: Lower engagement and retention with call summary feature
Recommended approach: Add WhatsApp deep link action chip using https://wa.me/<number> intent
Acceptance criteria: Tapping WhatsApp chip opens direct chat window with the caller in WhatsApp
Testing requirements: Complete call with phone number; tap WhatsApp action chip; verify WhatsApp opens direct chat

Current behavior: AnalyticsTracker interface implemented by FirebaseAnalyticsTracker and FakeAnalyticsTracker without schema validation
Expected behavior: Analytics events should validate parameters against a strict catalog schema prior to dispatch

Current behavior: AdLoadingDialog introduces a hardcoded delay(650) even when interstitial ad is already cached in memory
Expected behavior: Cached interstitial ads should display immediately without artificial delay once dialog renders

Business impact: Negative user perception; increases frustration with ad monetization

Current behavior: DynamicIslandPill.kt (5,705 lines) and PlaygroundScreen.kt (991 lines) mix UI, animation, and business logic

User impact: Difficult for multiple engineers to maintain; high risk of merge conflicts and regressions
Business impact: Slower engineering velocity; higher maintenance overhead
Recommended approach: Decompose DynamicIslandPill into CallSummaryIsland, TimerIsland, ActionControlIsland, SystemAlertsIsland, and PlaygroundCatalog
Acceptance criteria: Monolithic files decomposed; DynamicIslandPill reduced by 2
Confidence: 088 lines; zero compile or test regressions
Testing requirements: Medium

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 12] Unused NotificationReplyActivity Declared in Manifest
Current behavior: NotificationReplyActivity is declared in manifest but never launched by overlay or notifications
Expected behavior: Unused Activity declarations should be pruned or integrated into workflow
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 12. Integrated NotificationReplyActivity as reliable fallback quick-reply target when overlay focus is rejected by OEM window manager accessibility policies. Added createIntent(...) and launch(...) companion helpers. Overlay service automatically delegates to windowed NotificationReplyActivity if enableOverlayFocusable() fails. Unit tested in Sprint12DailyUtilityAndArchitectureTest.
Root cause: Confirmed: dead code Activity declaration
User impact: Unnecessary APK bloat and potential confusion for future engineers
Business impact: Minimal direct revenue impact; degrades codebase clarity and maintainability
Recommended approach: Integrate as fallback quick reply target when overlay accessibility focus is restricted by OEM policies
Acceptance criteria: Manifest declaration active; quick reply fallback functional across OEM policies
Testing requirements: Search codebase for all references; verify clean build after integration

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 11] Redundant Screen View Recording in Jetpack Compose Recompositions
Current behavior: AppScreen calls trackScreenView inside composition without DisposableEffect or LifecycleEventEffect guard
Expected behavior: Screen tracking should occur inside LifecycleEventEffect(Lifecycle.Event.ON_RESUME) to prevent recomposition duplicates
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 11. Integrated ScreenDeduplicator with LifecycleEventObserver(ON_RESUME) into AppScreen via TrackScreenView. Recompositions, theme toggles, and keyboard insets no longer trigger duplicate screen_view events. Verified on Realme 8 hardware logcat and in automated unit tests (Sprint11AnalyticsAndCrashlyticsTest). 36 analytics tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: analytics call executed during composition phase instead of lifecycle resume
User impact: Inflated screen_view metrics; skewed session duration and engagement analytics in GA4
Business impact: Misleading analytics reports; distorted user engagement statistics
Recommended approach: Move trackScreenView into ScreenDeduplicator or LifecycleEventEffect(ON_RESUME)
Acceptance criteria: Exactly 1 screen_view event recorded per screen navigation; 0 on recompositions
Testing requirements: Navigate to Settings; toggle theme 5 times; verify exactly 1 screen_view event in logcat

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 08] Paywall UI Deficiencies: Fabricated 'Save 70%' Discounts, Occluded Auto-Renewal Disclosures & Static White-Card Hero
Current behavior: Paywall showed fabricated 'Save 70%' discount badges without calculation base; static white card lacked interactive showcase; sticky bottom CTA occluded legal disclosures on small screens
Expected behavior: Paywall must display authentic value badges ('Most popular' / 'Lifetime access'); provide interactive Dynamic Island preview sandbox; provide transparent auto-renewal terms with guaranteed 140dp bottom scroll clearance
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 08. Replaced fabricated discounts with authentic badges across PlayBillingPremiumAccessGateway and SettingsVaultScreen. Added AuroraProHeroCard with interactive music/call/action sandbox and trial state awareness. Upgraded AppPlanSelectorRow and AppFreeVsProComparisonCard with AppleGlyph checks and cyan chips. Fixed bottom inset to 140dp for zero clipping. 325 unit tests pass. Verified on Realme 8 hardware.
Root cause: Confirmed: hardcoded 'Save 70%' discount string and insufficient bottom padding in Compose scroll container
User impact: Users distrusted misleading discount claims; auto-renewal terms occluded behind sticky button risking Play Store policy review rejection
Business impact: Direct conversion suppression and Google Play subscription policy enforcement risk
Recommended approach: Implement authentic badge policy; add interactive live sandbox; enforce 140dp bottomInset; redesign comparison matrix
Acceptance criteria: Zero fabricated discounts in billing catalog or UI; interactive island sandbox functional; disclosures scroll 100% clear of sticky CTA
Testing requirements: Execute full UI test suite and physical device verification on Realme 8; verify plan selector and disclosures

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 08A] Live Island Visual Weaknesses, Unconnected Reference States & Fake Demonstrations
Current behavior: Live Preview experiences (Delivery, Flight, Sports, Navigation) displayed misaligned typography, crude emojis, non-standard progress bars, and lacked real data mapping from Android NotificationListenerService or platform APIs
Expected behavior: All 36 reference states must be audited, classified honestly across 4 capability tiers (Fully Live, Conditionally Live, Preview Only, Unsupported); Delivery, Flight, Sports, and Navigation islands must feature pixel-perfect Apple-grade UI, structured metadata models, and real notification ingestion heuristics with strict Rule 31 zero-cricket compliance
Source evidence: app/src/main/java/ai/emots/kishan_dynamic/data/liveactivity/NotificationLiveActivityMapper.kt, LiveActivitiesScreen.kt, LiveIslandComponents.kt, DeliveryIsland.kt, FlightIsland.kt, SportsIsland.kt, NavigationIsland.kt, DynamicIslandPill.kt
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 08A. Implemented shared LiveIsland components with AppleGlyphs, milestone progress bars, live status badges, interactive intent actions (direct dial courier, launch Google Maps), and presentation toggle (Compact/Expanded). Real-time NotificationLiveActivityMapper extracts ETA, flight numbers, delivery stages, and football scores while strictly rejecting cricket notifications per Rule 31. Tested on Realme 8 hardware across dark and light themes. 334 unit tests pass.
Root cause: Confirmed: live preview used disconnected mock data and crude UI styling without routing to platform notification mapping or overlay renderer
User impact: Users experienced disjointed previews that did not match floating overlay behavior; unreadable sports and delivery layouts with overlapping text and crude emojis degraded perceived quality
Business impact: Suppressed user engagement with Live Activities; diminished perceived premium value of Aurora Dynamic Island
Recommended approach: Design and implement shared live island composables; connect NotificationLiveActivityMapper heuristics; wire presentation toggle and category filtering; enforce capability badges and real Android intents
Acceptance criteria: Pixel-perfect Delivery, Flight, Sports, and Navigation layouts; 36 reference states cataloged and classified; honest capability badges in UI; 100% unit tests pass; zero cricket compliance
Testing requirements: Execute LiveActivityFidelityAndMappingTest suite; deploy to physical device; capture screenshots across Compact/Expanded and light/dark modes

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 15] Active Notifications Evicted on Presentation Expiry Breaking Island Tapping
Current behavior: When a notification arrived, it auto-expanded for its presentation timer (4.5s) and then collapsed. However, upon collapse, the notification was completely evicted from notificationQueue, causing subsequent taps on the compact pill to open Quick Controls instead of re-expanding notifications
Expected behavior: Presentation timer must strictly control visual expansion (isExpanded = false) without evicting active notifications from memory; notifications must remain in queue until explicit user dismissal or source cancellation
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 15. Decoupled presentation expiry from queue retention. NotificationEvent.Expired returns state without deleting items. IslandStateManager.scheduleNotificationExpiry only sets isExpanded = false. Verified in NotificationReducerTest and on physical Realme 8 device.
Root cause: Confirmed: NotificationReducer purged items on NotificationEvent.Expired
User impact: Users lost access to inbound notifications once the heads-up display collapsed; tapping the compact pill failed to show notifications
Business impact: Severely degrades core product utility; breaks primary notification heads-up purpose
Recommended approach: Decouple visual expansion collapse from queue eviction; maintain notifications in memory until explicit dismissal
Acceptance criteria: Heads-up collapses cleanly after 4.5s; tapping compact pill reliably re-expands active card; 100% unit tests pass
Testing requirements: Deploy to physical device; simulate inbound messages; observe auto-collapse and subsequent single tap

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 15] Gesture Disambiguation: Single Tap on Minimal or Compact Launches Quick Controls
Current behavior: Single-tap and long-press interactions were entangled; single-tapping an idle Minimal island triggered Quick Controls sheet by accident; tapping compact island failed to route to active content
Expected behavior: Single tap on Minimal (idle) must strictly return IslandAction.None; long-press (>= 500ms) must be the exclusive, deliberate gateway to Quick Controls across all island states; single tap on compact expands active content
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 15. Updated IslandInteractionPolicy to return NONE for single tap on Minimal state. Established main long-press as exclusive trigger for ActionControl. Single tap on compact with active notifications re-expands card. Verified in IslandInteractionPolicyTest (10 tests pass) and on Realme 8.
Root cause: Confirmed: IslandInteractionPolicy.mainTap returned OPEN_QUICK_CONTROLS on Minimal state
User impact: Users accidentally launched intrusive system controls sheet when trying to tap background apps or idle island; impossible to interact predictably
Business impact: Frustrates users; creates perception of buggy overlay interference
Recommended approach: Return NONE on Minimal tap; dedicate long press exclusively to Quick Controls; route compact tap to content expand
Acceptance criteria: Zero accidental sheet launches on tap; long press reliably opens Quick Controls; compact tap re-expands tasks
Testing requirements: Test single tap and long press on physical Realme 8 device across idle and active states

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 15] Clipping Intermediate Black Box Artifact During Compact-Expanded Morph
Current behavior: Transitions between compact (36.67dp) and expanded (210dp) suffered from a jarring visual artifact where child content rendered immediately, causing clipping inside an intermediate black box before WindowManager bounds settled
Expected behavior: Child content must remain invisible during the initial expansion phase until the container capsule has morphed past 70% of its target height; exiting content must fade out rapidly before container starts shrinking
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 15. Staggered child content entrance in AppMotion.islandContentEnter with 110ms delay (delayMillis = 110). Reduced exit transition to 80ms fast fade out. Layout-phase animated dimensions bypass composition. Verified on Realme 8.
Root cause: Confirmed: child content entered at t=0 while container dimensions were still animating via spring physics
User impact: Visual distortion and black box tearing during state expansion degraded perceived aesthetic quality
Business impact: Damages Apple-grade liquid motion polish
Recommended approach: Stagger content enter by 110ms; exit by 80ms; maintain layout-phase measurement
Acceptance criteria: Zero intermediate black clipping; 60fps liquid spring morphing; clean content reveal
Testing requirements: Perform 50 consecutive morph transitions on physical device; inspect frame pacing and visual clipping

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 15] Floating Island Overlay Physically Occludes In-App Navigation Headers
Current behavior: Floating Dynamic Island overlay physically overlapped Aurora's own app headers (AppLargeTitle and AppTopBar), partially obscuring titles like 'Dynamic Island', 'Action Island', and back buttons
Expected behavior: App screens must provide generous top clearance below the camera notch and floating overlay so headers and navigation buttons never collide with the island
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 15. Increased AppLargeTitle top padding from 20dp to 44dp and AppTopBar top padding from 12dp to 28dp in AppKit.kt. Verified on Realme 8 hardware in sprint15_realme_home_unlocked.png.
Root cause: Confirmed: fixed 20dp/12dp padding failed to account for 36.67dp compact island + status bar height
User impact: In-app titles and navigation controls were occluded
Business impact: causing ugly visual overlap on first launch
Recommended approach: Unprofessional first impression; potential navigation occlusion
Dependencies: Increase top padding on AppLargeTitle to 44dp and AppTopBar to 28dp
Acceptance criteria: S (1h)
Confidence: Titles and back buttons sit comfortably clear below floating island overlay; verified on hardware
Testing requirements: High
column18: Capture screenshot on Realme 8 hardware; inspect header clearance across all root and detail screens

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 15] Quick Controls Expanded Sheet Clamps at 180dp Clipping Volume & Brightness Sliders
Current behavior: Quick Controls expanded card had a cramped 180dp fixed height, causing bottom sliders (Volume and Brightness) to be clipped off at the bottom edge; system chips clipped labels ('Auto b...', 'Locat...')
Expected behavior: Card height must accommodate 2 slider rows and a 4-tile grid comfortably; chips must have sufficient width, padding, and text ellipsis
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 15. Increased ActionControlExpanded base height to 210dp with 58dp per-row spacing. Widened QuickControlChip from 58dp to 62dp with horizontal padding and TextOverflow.Ellipsis. Verified on Realme 8.
Root cause: Confirmed: hardcoded 180dp height was insufficient for 2 slider rows and 4 chips
User impact: Users could not see full volume/brightness sliders; truncated chip labels made quick actions ambiguous
Business impact: Degraded daily utility and polish of system quick controls
Recommended approach: Increase expanded height to 210dp; widen chips to 62dp; add ellipsis
Acceptance criteria: Full slider throw visible; chip labels legible without truncation; verified on hardware
Testing requirements: Open Quick Controls on physical device; inspect vertical and horizontal boundaries

Summary: [RESOLVED IN SPRINT 15] WhatsApp Upload Progress Displays Generic Charging Lightning & Redundant Text
Current behavior: WhatsApp file upload tasks in expanded island rendered with a generic green lightning icon (charging glyph), duplicate 'WhatsApp / WhatsApp' labeling, and an oversized container
Expected behavior: Upload progress must show the authentic application package icon; title and subtitle must be distinct; container height must match content
Runtime evidence: Verified & Resolved in Sprint 15. Replaced hardcoded AppleGlyph.Charging in NotificationProgressCard with PackageIcon(notification.packageName). Deduped text to show appName as caption and distinct text as title.
Root cause: Confirmed: hardcoded AppleGlyph.Charging in NotificationProgressCard and redundant title fallback
User impact: Confused users into thinking phone was charging; repetitive text degraded visual craft
Business impact: Diminished perceived quality of Dynamic Island notification representation
Recommended approach: Replace glyph with PackageIcon; deduplicate title/caption logic
Acceptance criteria: Authentic app icon displayed; clean progress bar and distinct title text
Testing requirements: Trigger file upload progress notification; verify icon and text layout on device
